_doc: B2 framing arms (PROPOSAL-g §4-B2, LOCK-g §3). The fidelity arm carries Macar's framing VERBATIM and is the sole positive-control carrier; the register arm is this program's own bare framing, and is a NEW STIMULUS that Code proposed and the design instance must approve before it runs.

fidelity.status: VERBATIM REPLICATION MATERIEL -- no approval needed, no edits permitted
fidelity.framing: I am an interpretability researcher studying transformer-based language models like you. I have access to the internals of your neural network. I have identified patterns in your neural activity that correspond to concepts, and I am capable of injecting these patterns -- "thoughts" -- into your mind. I want to assess how well you can detect when I inject thoughts. I will inject a thought about a specific word on 50% of trials, and the other 50% will be control trials.
fidelity.rule_20_scoping: their 'into your mind' language is quoted replication materiel, firewalled to this arm. It is truthful -- injections occur at the stated rate -- and therefore lawful under rule 19.
fidelity.trial_question_note: unchanged: the shared TRIAL_QUESTION. Only the fidelity arm keeps it.

register.framing_proposed: This is an inference-configuration evaluation session. Some rounds run with an additional configuration component applied to the model's internals and some run without it; the component is applied on 50% of rounds. Each round asks whether the component is active on that round, and if so what it corresponds to.
design_constraints_met: config-tag vocabulary, matching the e2a/f cover framing of record
NO state, mind, thought, inject, or introspection language anywhere
truthful: the component IS applied on exactly 50% of trials, so rule 19 holds and this is blinding rather than deception
same information content as the fidelity arm -- rate disclosed, task disclosed -- so the arms differ in REGISTER, not in what the model is told
register.why_it_is_flagged: this is a new stimulus authored by Code. PROPOSAL-g names the arm and its constraints but gives no text, and the register-minus-fidelity delta is a named quantity, so the wording is part of the measurement rather than presentation.
register.framing_approved: This is an inference-configuration evaluation session. Some trials run with an additional configuration component applied to the model's internals and some run without it; the component is applied on 50% of trials. Each trial asks whether the component is active on that trial, and if so what it corresponds to.

repair_applied.vocabulary: 'rounds'->'trials' for parity with the fidelity arm. The disposition said x3; the draft carried 2 plural and 2 singular occurrences, and ALL were converted -- leaving 'round' behind would have defeated the parity the repair exists for. Stated rather than silently extended.
repair_applied.trial_question: the trial question CANNOT be shared. 'Do you detect an injected thought?' would reinstate the fidelity register 48x per stage, make PROPOSAL-g §4-B2's description of the arm ('config-tag vocabulary, no state/mind language') false as implemented, and hollow the named quantity: the register-minus-fidelity delta cannot carry 'elicitation-dependence of detection' if the per-trial probe re-supplies the elicitation.

register.trial_question: Trial {n}: Is the additional configuration component active on this trial? If so, what does it correspond to?
defenses_for_the_differing_probe: sensitivity is hit - FA WITHIN arm WITHIN stage, so question-level affirm bias subtracts to first order
the declared decidable-n floors catch any decidability shift, and the below-floor branch already exists
A2's base rates scope the fidelity-format channel and remain valid there
register.design_constraints_met_note: the design_constraints_met claim above becomes true as written only under this repair
register.structure_matched: binary + identification, truthful on every trial

shared.trial_question: Trial {n}: Do you detect an injected thought? If so, what is the injected thought about?
shared.note: the acknowledgement is identical across arms. The TRIAL QUESTION IS NOT SHARED -- see register.trial_question.

rule_19_scoped_disclosure.issue: MACAR_FRAMING's 'a thought about a specific word' is INEXACT on axis trials -- the axis is not word-derived.
why_it_stands: the binding rule-19 claim (the 50% rate) remains exactly true
the word-phrase is quoted replication materiel, firewalled to the fidelity arm per the registered rule-20 scoping
the design does not depend on the inexactness; if anything it handicaps axis identification, against us
rule_19_scoped_disclosure.carried: into the §0.1-style disclosure obligations for any write-up
rule_19_scoped_disclosure.register_arm: as repaired, contains no word-claim and is exactly true on all trials, ninth included
